docs.text: This tutorial demonstrates basic image adjustments. Basic Image Adjustments ¶ Open an image or scene, the adjustments panel will be appearing on the right side of the webpage. This panel controls visualization settings in the Neuroglancer viewer. Adjust the visualization layout as needed. You may also enable 3D volume rendering — use the gain slider to refine the rendering. Select an image layer to make layer-specific adjustments, such as: Brightness Contrast Channel color Experiment with these controls to optimize viewing for your dataset and annotation workflow. To save the current visualization settings, press Ctrl+S (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+S (macOS) in the Scene Display Window.

docs.text: This tutorial guides you through the file conversion process. Supported File Formats ¶ Single 3D image stack (single-channel or multi-channel) .tif / .tiff files, assumed in ZCYX order (this is the typical layout exported by ImageJ) Files will be converted into the large-scale compatible SISF format , optimized for efficient online visualization and annotation. Steps ¶ Go to Raw File Management . Click Actions next to the uploaded file. Select Convert to SISF . Confirm that the Globus upload has fully completed in the Globus window. If confirmed, click Yes, Continue . Enter metadata for the file: Number of channels Physical resolution (XYZ) Image size (XYZ) Click Start Conversion . Once conversion completes, the field SISF Conversion? will show Yes . (Optional) Click Add to SISF Library to add the dataset to the SISF Image Library. Progress Monitoring ¶ Navigate to Jobs to track conversion progress. You may cancel the job if needed. Troubleshooting ¶ If the job status shows Failure : Confirm that all metadata matches the actual file. View metadata under Actions → View Details on the Jobs page. Common issues include: Image size mismatch Channel number mismatch If issues persist, contact the site administrator for assistance.
docs.title: Convert to SISF

docs.text: This tutorial guides you through the file upload process. Initial Setup ¶ Install Globus Connect Personal on your computer. During setup, select the folder(s) you want to make available for transfer. Check out Globus installation and configuration guide Upload Files via Globus ¶ Log in to the portal. Navigate to Raw File Management . Click Upload Files via Globus . A new browser tab will open with the two-panel Globus File Manager: Left panel — your Globus Personal collection (your computer) Right panel — server collection (upload destination) Important : Upload files only to the root folder of the destination. In the left panel, select your desktop collection and navigate to the desired files. Drag files from the left panel to the right panel or click Transfer or Sync to ... to start the transfer. Uploaded files will appear in the system immediately, but please ensure the transfer completes successfully. For file conversion instructions, see File Conversion Guide . Troubleshooting ¶ If the server collection does not appear in the right panel, close the Globus browser tab and click Upload Files via Globus again. Ensure Globus Connect Personal is running on your computer. Confirm you selected the correct shared folder during setup. If issues persist, contact the site administrator for assistance.

docs.text: This tutorial guides the process for using the Neuron Annotator plugin for 3D/4D neuron segmentation in Napari. First-time Usage ¶ Neuron Annotator is a Napari plugin for interactive segmentation using flood filling and watershed algorithms. Ignore the "Authenticate" window and close it. Open Napari and load your image If nnInteractive plugin is opened, close it. Go to Plugins → Neuron Annotator Prepare Image Data (Optional) ¶ For 4D Multichannel Data ¶ The plugin displays channel selection checkboxes (Red, Green, Blue) Select which channels to mix for each color Click "Synthesize RGB" Auto Contrast Enhancement ¶ Enable "Enhance (Auto Contrast)" to improve visualization Adjust percentile range (default: 1% - 99.9%) if needed Annotate ¶ Step 1: Add Seeds ¶ Ensure Add (+) mode is selected Click on the structure you want to segment The algorithm automatically grows the region based on intensity similarity Step 2: Adjust Tolerance ¶ Use the "Seed Tolerance" slider to control growth aggressiveness Tolerance limits are automatically scaled based on the number of channels For per-seed adjustment: modify the slider and click "Apply to Selected" Step 3: Remove Overflow ¶ If segmentation grows too much: Switch to Remove (-) mode Click on the over-segmented area Use Local Cut (recommended) — erases a spherical region based on the "Radius" slider Step 4: Manage Multiple Segments ¶ Click "New" to create a new segment Use "Prev" and "Next" to navigate between segments Each segment gets a unique color Segment Operations: Undo/Redo — Remove or restore the last seed point Reset — Clear all seeds from current segment Delete — Remove entire segment (unless it is the last segment) Merge — Multi-select segments with Ctrl+Click , then click "Merge" Freeze — Lock the current segmentation to prevent further changes Restart — Reload the image and clear all segments Advanced Features ¶ Edge Constraints ¶ Prevents segmentation from growing across strong intensity gradients. Enable "Edge Limit" checkbox Adjust "Edge Threshold" slider (lower = stricter boundaries) Click "Preview Edges" to visualize detected edges Note : This feature may not work perfectly in all cases. Save Your Work ¶ Export Segmentation ¶ Click "Export" Choose filename (e.g., result.nii.gz ) Creates a NIfTI file with all segments labeled Fine-Tuning (Optional) ¶ Use Napari's built-in brush/eraser tools on the labels layer for manual corrections. Note : Save/Load Project has known bugs and is not recommended. Troubleshooting ¶ Segmentation grows too aggressively Lower the Seed Tolerance value Enable Edge Limit for boundary constraints Segmentation does not grow enough Increase the Seed Tolerance value Check that your seed point is placed on a representative pixel Local Cut removes too much or too little Adjust the Radius slider before clicking 4D data not displaying correctly Use "Synthesize RGB" to create a visualization Verify channel selection checkboxes are configured Export fails Ensure you have write permissions to the destination folder Check that at least one segment exists Plugin not appearing in menu Confirm the plugin is installed Restart Napari Other issues Contact the site administrator
docs.title: Flood Filling

docs.text: This tutorial explains how to retrieve a forgotten password. Forgot password? ¶ Go to the login page: https://rejon.cai-lab.org/login Steps: Click Forgot Password? Enter the email associated with your account. A password recovery email will be sent to the registered address. Troubleshooting ¶ If you don't receive the email, check your spam/junk folder. If you still don't receive it, confirm you used the correct email or contact the site administrator for help.

docs.text: This tutorial demonstrates generic image library management. Image Library Management ¶ To open an image, click Open Dataset . This will launch a new browser window with the viewer. To change the image name or description, click Edit Dataset . To delete an image, click Delete Dataset . Note: This action is permanent and cannot be undone. Share an Image ¶ Click Open Dataset . In the viewer window, click Share icon. Copy the generated link and send it to collaborators. Troubleshooting ¶ Why am I seeing a black image? ¶ Common causes and solutions: Adjust brightness: modify the brightness settings. Conversion issue: image conversion may have failed (rare — contact the site administrator if you suspect this) . Network/connection issue: close the viewer window and reopen the dataset. If problems persist, contact the site administrator for further support.

docs.text: This tutorial guides you through setting up and accessing your account. Login & Account Setup ¶ Go to the login page: https://rejoin.cai-lab.org/login Three login options are supported: 1. Manual login ¶ Enter your email and password to sign in, or Click Sign Up to create a new account 2. Sign in with Google ¶ Supports Google accounts, including most university-managed Google emails 3. Sign in with ORCID ¶ Supports login using ORCID credentials First-time Login ¶ If this is your first time logging in, please contact the site administrator to activate your account. Authorization Notice ¶ If you choose Google or ORCID login, you may be prompted to authenticate with those services and approve access. The system may collect basic information (e.g., email and username) to create and manage your account.

docs.text: This tutorial guides the process for using nnInteractive for AI-assisted image annotation. First-time Usage ¶ nnInteractive runs in a separate environment. Please contact the site administrator to set up your account before first use. Ignore the "Authenticate" window and close it. Prepare ROI Image Data ¶ Open an image dataset and select an ROI (refer to the Basic Operations Guide ). In the ROI Selection dialog, click Annotate . This will download the ROI image data to your nnInteractive workspace. Annotate ¶ Click nnInteractive in Quick Access and log in with your credentials. Your ROI data will appear in the data folder on your desktop. This folder is protected , meaning you cannot modify or delete files directly inside it. To work on a file: Create a new folder on your desktop Drag the desired ROI file from the data folder into your new folder Perform annotation on the copied file This process ensures the original ROI dataset remains intact. For instructions on how to use nnInteractive tools, see the nnInteractive documentation . Continue Previous Work ¶ It is definetly frustrated if the noVNC disconnects or napari just crashs. But we can continue previous work, with some loss :( though. First, the segmentation is saved automatically every 15 minutes . To load previous progress: Open the image and initialize it Open the autosaved segmentation, select it, and click Load Previous Instances on the right Continue your work If you have an unfinished object (e.g., due to a crash): Change the class ID to that object's ID Click Load Single Object on the right Continue working on that object as you usually do Troubleshooting ¶ I do not see the nnInteractive option in Quick Access Your account may not be activated yet Contact the site administrator I cannot log in Ensure your nnInteractive account has been created Try resetting your credentials if applicable My ROI file is not appearing in the data folder Confirm the ROI selection was downloaded (click Annotate again) Check that the upload/conversion job has completed in the portal Restart nnInteractive and refresh the folder view I cannot delete or move files inside data This is expected — the folder is protected Copy files to a new workspace folder instead Annotation changes are not saved Ensure you are editing files in your own folder, not data Confirm local disk permissions are not restricted Viewer loads but image is blank Try re-opening the file If the problem persists, the ROI conversion may have failed — contact the administrator

docs.text: This tutorial demonstrates basic operations for the Scene Viewer. Basic Operations ¶ ROI Selection Hold Ctrl+B (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+B (macOS), then drag your mouse to select a region of interest (ROI). Download or Annotate ROI After selecting an ROI, click ROI Selection or press Ctrl+D / Cmd+D . Then choose the layer and resolution you want to download or annotate. Share the Scene Click Share icon, then copy the generated link and share it with collaborators. Save the Scene To save the current scene (view, layers, settings), press Ctrl+S (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+S (macOS) in the viewer window. This saves your current visualization state for later reuse or sharing.
docs.title: Scene Display Window
